title: code-review brain dump: batcher + kv-cache refactors
body:
Objective: quick, messy scratchpad for PR review items on the runtime batcher + kv cache changes. Use this to collect review comments, follow-ups, and micro-refactors I want to file after reading the PR and running a couple local profiles. Not a polished doc — just thoughts to land into issues/mini-PRs later.

High-level notes from reading PR (runtime/pull/1324):
- Adds dynamic batch sizing heuristics based on recent seq-len distribution.
- Integrates prefix-based KV cache invalidation for model variant pins.
- Changes Batcher API: Batcher.enqueue(Request, priority_hint) -> now returns future + batch_meta token.
- Some new instrumented metrics (batch_util_p95, batch_latency_by_len).

Immediate review checklist (things to assert or call out in comments):
- [ ] Correctness: ensure kv-cache invalidation does not leak across pinned variants. Check test coverage for variant-switch scenarios.
- [ ] Backwards compatibility: Batcher API changed — verify all call sites updated (console routing, dedicated runner, private agent). Search repo for direct .enqueue(...) usages.
- [ ] Thread-safety: dynamic sizing touches shared histograms; ensure locks are minimal and no global locking under hot path.
- [ ] Metrics cardinality: batch_latency_by_len must bucket lengths; ensure label cardinality capped (e.g., 0..1024 to buckets) — watch for unbounded labels.
- [ ] Observability: new metrics are exposed to tracing; add span annotations when batch resized (want to correlate trace->resize).

Quick run notes (local profile):
- On local model with synthetic load, observed a tail of small batches after resizing kicks in; likely because the sizing heuristic uses an EWMA with slow decay, causing oscillation.
- Memory: KV entries were not freed for variant switch in small repro. Confirm: I ran variant-switch test and saw stale cache entries lingering for ~6s before GC.

Concrete review comments to post on PR: (copy/paste ready)
1) "The new dynamic batcher uses a single global histogram (batch_len_hist). For multi-tenant requests we should namespace histograms by tenant or route (or at least by model family). Can we either include a route label with bounded buckets, or make the histogram per-batcher instance? High-cardinality labels will blow out Pushgateway/TSDB."

2) "KV cache invalidation: I couldn't find a unit test exercising the case where a request is in-flight while the pinned variant toggles. Please add a test where Request A is enqueued on variant V1, then route updated to V2 and a new request arrives — ensure A still uses V1's KV and doesn't read V2's entries."

3) "The Batcher.enqueue signature change is breaking and scattered changes in the codebase are easy to miss. Suggest adding a transitional overload or adapter for 1 release cycle to avoid runtime surprises in Dedicated agents that might be on older agent versions."

4) "Sizing heuristic: the EWMA decay constant appears to be hard-coded at 0.9 in code. Recommend making this configurable via runtime config with sane defaults and a knob per-deployment (hosted vs dedicated). Also add a simple unit test that simulates a sudden spike and ensures the heuristic doesn't oscillate more than N times."

Micro-refactors / follow-ups to file as issues:
- FR-1: "batcher: split histogram + heuristic into a separate module". Rationale: makes it easier to unit test heuristics and to swap in alternate algorithms (RL-based or PID) later.
- FR-2: "kv-cache: add strong ownership metadata to entries (variant_id, model_hash, route_id) and add TTL+eager prune path when variant pinned change occurs."

Potential perf regressions to validate in CI:
- Increased CPU on hot path due to histogram updates (atomic ops) — add microbench.
- Latency spikes when batch resize runs concurrently with heavy enqueue — add stress CI with high QPS and short sequences.

Lines in-code that caught my eye (file/line hints):
- runtime/batcher/dynamic_sizing.py:42-88 — tight loop updating histogram, missing an early exit if predicted target matches current for >3 windows.
- runtime/kv/variant_cache.py:113 — invalidate_variants() iterates map without holding lock on mutation path (dangerous).
- runtime/server/request_router.py:204 — assumes enqueue returns future only; new meta token ignored causing telemetry mismatch.

Ideas for tests to add (straightforward):
- unit: simulate 3 tenants with different seq-len distributions; ensure per-tenant batching decisions don't affect each other if configured to be isolated.
- integration: variant switch during in-flight request: orchestrate two requests, flip pin mid-flight, assert cache isolation.
- perf: microbench to measure atomic histogram update cost per-enqueue across 8 threads.

UI/ops follow-ups:
- Add dashboard row for "batch_resize_events" with top routes causing resizes. Right now it's opaque.
- Add an alert if batch_util_p95 drops >20% vs last 24h for a route (could indicate over-aggressive resizing).

Notes-to-self (things I might implement quickly):
- Small PR to add an adapter overload for Batcher.enqueue that maintains old signature and logs deprecation once — reduces blast radius.
- File an issue to add a safety test in the dedicated-agent e2e that runs against the latest runtime but older agent to simulate partial rollout.

Open questions / TODOs (need answers from author):
- Why is the EWMA constant 0.9? historical note? (ask Diego)
- Are we happy with per-route or per-tenant histograms? Might prefer per-route for visibility but per-tenant for isolation.
- Can variant pin changes be scheduled off the hot path to avoid invalidating while requests are being routed? If not, need stronger locking semantics.

Prioritization (my current view):
1) Safety tests for variant-switch isolation (high priority).
2) Transitional overload for enqueue API (quick safety).
3) Reduce metric cardinality risk (medium).
4) Perf microbench and lock audit (medium).

Last note: keep this doc around until I either open the follow-up issues or close them; marking as draft for now.

End of dump.
